simple.meaning: חָרַם (châram) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to seclude ; specifically (by a ban) to devote to religious uses (especially destruction); physical and reflexive, to be blunt as to the nose.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 52 times across Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, and 11 more, beginning at Exodus 22:19. Its contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָרַם (H2763).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חָרַם (châram) / H2763 is traced through Exodus 22:19, Leviticus 21:18, Leviticus 27:28, Leviticus 27:29 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to seclude ; specifically (by a ban) to devote to religious uses (especially destruction); physical and reflexive, to be blunt as to the nose
